Russia must agree to a winter ceasefire on energy infrastructure and a truce ensuring the safe passage of food exports through the Black Sea, she said — steps that would show Moscow is serious about negotiations. Brussels will judge progress 'by Russia's actions, not just by its words', von der Leyen added. A 'strong European team' will join the next round of talks, including representatives of Germany, France, Britain, Italy and Poland, as well as the European Commission and the European Council. She noted that the EU has provided Ukraine with more than 235 billion euros since the start of the full-scale invasion and plans to send a further 45 billion euros in 2027. Moscow reacted coolly: Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov dismissed the statement as 'megaphone diplomacy', and Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov said there is still no understanding of when the next round of talks between Russia, the US and Ukraine will take place. The announcement matters because it marks Europe's formal entry into a peace process that Washington and Moscow have so far conducted largely without it.

articles.title: Ukraine hits five Russian warplanes at Savasleyka airbase — three MiG-31s and two Su-34s
articles.description: Ukrainian forces have struck Russia's Savasleyka airbase, damaging five warplanes — three MiG-31 jets that carry hypersonic Kinzhal missiles and two Su-34 fighter-bombers — the General Staff said on November 25. The base is about 300 kilometres east of Moscow, and the damaged aircraft will be unable to fly for some time. Russia has not commented.
articles.body: Ukrainian forces have struck a major Russian military airbase, damaging five warplanes used to launch missiles and bombs at Ukraine, the General Staff said on November 25. The Savasleyka airbase in the Nizhny Novgorod region, about 300 kilometres east of Moscow, was hit overnight on November 24–25. Three MiG-31 jets — the carriers of hypersonic Kinzhal missiles fired at Ukrainian cities — and two Su-34 fighter-bombers were damaged, and the General Staff said the aircraft would be 'unable to fly for some time'. Damage assessments are ongoing and the exact number of affected aircraft is being clarified; Russia has not commented. Savasleyka is one of the key bases for Russia's long-range strike aviation, and the MiG-31s based there are among the most threatening aircraft in Russia's arsenal, since Kinzhals are among the hardest missiles for Ukrainian air defences to intercept. The same day, the General Staff reported a strike on a P-18 long-range radar near Karavan-Solodkyi in occupied Luhansk region, plus hits on fuel depots and logistics facilities in Luhansk and Donetsk regions. The strikes are part of Ukraine's systematic campaign against the Russian military machine deep behind the front lines, carried out even as US-led peace talks continue.

articles.title: Brooklyn jury finds Huawei guilty on 10 of 12 counts in trade-secrets case
articles.description: A jury in Brooklyn has found Huawei guilty on 10 of 12 counts, including conspiracy to steal trade secrets and bank fraud over its business in Iran, the US Justice Department said. The company was acquitted on the racketeering count. The verdict caps a case first brought in 2019 and is a major win for Washington in its confrontation with the Chinese telecoms giant.
articles.body: A jury in Brooklyn has found Chinese telecoms giant Huawei guilty on 10 of 12 counts, including conspiracy to steal trade secrets and bank fraud over its business in Iran, the US Justice Department said. The jury acquitted the company on the racketeering count. The verdict, reported in Ukrainian media on November 25, is the culmination of a case first brought in 2019, when US prosecutors accused Huawei of stealing technology from American rivals, including T-Mobile's phone-testing robot, and of misleading banks about its operations in Iran in breach of sanctions. Huawei has denied wrongdoing throughout. The conviction is a significant win for Washington in its long-running confrontation with Huawei, which the US has treated as a national-security threat and largely shut out of American networks and supply chains. It also lands at a sensitive moment in US-China relations, as the Trump administration weighs new tariffs on China and other trading partners. For the global telecoms industry, the verdict reinforces the legal risks of doing business with sanctioned countries — and the reach of US courts over foreign companies.

articles.title: UPDATE: Take-Two cracks down on GTA VI PC port efforts, removing thousands of GitHub repositories
articles.description: Take-Two Interactive has moved against the unofficial PC port of Grand Theft Auto VI, with its lawyers hunting down the enthusiast teams behind it and getting several thousand repositories removed from GitHub. The crackdown follows the leak of the game's key executable file on November 23. It is the latest escalation in the cat-and-mouse game around the biggest launch in gaming history.
articles.body: Take-Two Interactive has begun a legal crackdown on the unofficial PC port of Grand Theft Auto VI, GameMAG reports. The company's lawyers are now targeting the enthusiast teams working on the port, and have had several thousand repositories removed from GitHub. The move comes after a hacker group published a working Xbox Series X|S build of the game on November 19, and the key executable file — the piece needed to actually run and modify the game — leaked online on November 23. That leak opened the door to an unofficial PC version built with the help of AI tools to patch and adapt the files, and pirates have been racing to get it running. Take-Two's response has been swift and sweeping, going after the code repositories that host the porting tools and files. The episode echoes earlier leak battles around GTA VI, including the major 2022 leak of early footage, and shows how aggressively Rockstar's parent company protects its biggest asset. A PC version of GTA VI has not been announced, and Rockstar has historically taken a year or more to bring its games to PC. Until then, the unofficial port remains the only way to play on PC — and Take-Two is determined to keep it that way.

articles.title: UPDATE: Army detonates nearly five tons of unstable explosives in Iowa after days of legal and political wrangling
articles.description: The US Army carried out its planned controlled detonation of nearly five tons of unstable lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant near Middletown on Wednesday morning, November 25. The blast went ahead at 9 a.m. CT after a federal appeals court reinstated the EPA permit and President Trump dropped his hold. Residents within five miles to the southwest were evacuated, while those within 5–20 miles were told to stay indoors.
articles.body: The US Army detonated nearly five tons of deteriorating lead azide explosives at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant near Middletown, Iowa, on Wednesday morning, November 25, ending days of legal and political wrangling over the operation. The controlled detonation took place at 9 a.m. CT and was felt as a percussion wave across the area, with a large plume of smoke rising from the site. The blast was meant to dispose of 68 barrels of lead azide — a volatile material used to detonate munitions — that had become dangerously unstable after long-term storage at the World War II-era plant, which spans about 19,000 acres in rural Des Moines County. Army officials said a controlled detonation was far preferable to an uncontrolled one, warning that cold weather could cause the material to explode spontaneously. To contain lead dust, the Army built sand barriers and two-storey-high water walls around the site and used water and gel blocks and foam to absorb the blast. The operation had originally been scheduled for November 20, was postponed to November 23, then paused on Monday after President Trump ordered a halt until the courts and Iowa's governor-elect approved it; a federal appeals court reinstated the EPA permit on Monday evening and the Army announced it would proceed. FEMA sent an imminent-threat alert to phones in the area on Tuesday, and residents within five miles southwest of the plant were offered evacuation help, while those within 5–20 miles were told to stay indoors with windows closed. Environmental groups and local residents had protested the plan, fearing lead contamination of soil, water and farmland, and the EPA is testing air and soil before and after the blast. The timing — the day before Thanksgiving — drew particular criticism from residents who felt uninformed about safety and cleanup.

articles.title: Trump targets China and the EU in a new round of tariffs after the Supreme Court struck down his earlier ones
articles.description: President Donald Trump is preparing a new round of tariffs on China and dozens of other countries, seeking to revive his trade agenda after the Supreme Court struck down the sweeping global tariffs he introduced earlier this year. China faces a proposed starting rate of 20%, which could rise to 40%, while the EU would start at 15% and could go to 20%. The earliest the tariffs could take effect is January.
articles.body: President Donald Trump is preparing to impose a new round of tariffs on China and dozens of other countries, in an effort to revive his trade agenda after the Supreme Court struck down the sweeping global tariffs he introduced earlier this year. China is set to face the highest proposed rate among the 14 trading partners targeted by the investigation, starting at 20% and potentially rising to 40% if other factors, including ongoing trade negotiations and agreements between Washington and Beijing, fall away, a senior White House official told reporters late Tuesday. The European Union's proposed starting rate would be 15%, rising to 20% if pre-existing trade agreements are not honoured. The earliest the administration expects the tariffs to take effect is January, the official said. The move reopens a trade confrontation that had defined much of Trump's economic policy, and it comes despite polling showing the tariffs are unpopular: two-thirds of voters said Trump's tariffs hurt the national economy, according to nationwide results of CNN's voter poll. The announcement also comes as Trump took credit for getting Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO on Monday, despite bipartisan concerns about whether China is using advanced Nvidia chips to bolster its military capabilities by bypassing export restrictions. For businesses, the prospect of fresh tariffs on China and Europe — the two largest US trading partners — means renewed uncertainty over supply chains and prices just as the holiday shopping season peaks. Beijing and Brussels have not yet formally responded, but both have retaliated against previous rounds, raising the prospect of another cycle of tit-for-tat measures.

articles.title: Disney sued by NFL agent Zac Hiller's LAA Music over alleged unlicensed music in ESPN, Hulu, Disney Parks and FX promos
articles.description: The Walt Disney Company is being sued for allegedly using unlicensed music in at least seven promotional videos on social media, including on TikTok and Instagram. The lawsuit, filed on November 24 in the US District Court for the Eastern District of Michigan by publishing company LAA Music and its owner, NFL agent Zac Hiller, claims four Disney businesses — ESPN, Hulu, Disney Parks and FX — used three works the plaintiffs say they own without a licence. 'Disney never asked for a license. Disney never paid a dollar,' the complaint states.
articles.body: The Walt Disney Company is being sued for allegedly using unlicensed music in at least seven promotional videos on social media, including on TikTok and Instagram, in a lawsuit filed on Tuesday, November 24, in the US District Court for the Eastern District of Michigan by publishing company LAA Music and its owner, NFL agent Zac Hiller. The 23-page complaint claims four Disney businesses — ESPN, Hulu, Disney Parks and FX — used, without a licence, three works the plaintiffs say they own, and opens: 'For a hundred years, The Walt Disney Company has taught the world one rule: if you want to use what someone else created, you ask permission and you pay. Disney enforces that rule against everyone else. This case is about Disney exempting itself from it.' One Hulu promotion alone drew roughly 481,700 likes and 17,500 shares, according to the filing. The plaintiffs say they gave Disney written notice of each use starting in August 2026, and that for two months Disney's legal department answered only 'under review', at one point blaming an unnamed 'Dutch company' for two of the videos, before all seven videos came down. The complaint argues that taking a video down after being caught 'does not undo the infringement', and that the music licences held by TikTok and Instagram do not cover brand advertising. The seven videos include three on ESPN's accounts using a beat by producer Soumadethis later used in Sha Gz's 2022 track 'New Opp', a Hulu TikTok by 'Abbott Elementary' star Janelle James set to Trayvon Jackson's 'Gang Gang', two Disney Parks videos posted by creators under Disney's 'Non-Obligated Influencers' programme, and an FX Instagram post promoting 'The Drop: A Snowfall Saga'. LAA does not specify a damages figure, seeking the licence fees Disney would have paid plus any profits, or alternatively statutory damages of up to $150,000 per work if infringement is found wilful — a $450,000 ceiling across the three works, though five of the seven videos were posted before the works were registered with the US Copyright Office, which can rule out statutory damages and legal fees. The suit is the latest in a wave of cases over music in social-media marketing, following a federal judge's refusal on November 23 to dismiss Warner Music Group's lawsuit against shoe retailer DSW, and it cites 2022 rulings against energy drink brand Bang Energy in cases brought by Universal and Sony.

articles.title: UPDATE: Police say 'unknown substance' at Don Toliver's Manchester show may be linked to arena robberies
articles.description: British police said on Tuesday they are investigating whether the release of an 'unknown substance' at Don Toliver's concert at Manchester's Co-op Live arena on Sunday was linked to a small number of robberies at the show. Greater Manchester Police said they had received nine reports of jewellery being stolen during the concert, and that 'detectives are exploring the possibility that release of the substance could be linked'. Around 12,000 people were evacuated from the arena and nearly 90 showed symptoms, though only one person was taken to hospital.
articles.body: British police said on Tuesday they are investigating whether the release of an 'unknown substance' at Don Toliver's concert at Manchester's Co-op Live arena on Sunday night was linked to a small number of robberies at the show. Greater Manchester Police said the force had received nine reports of jewellery being stolen during the concert, adding in a statement that 'detectives are exploring the possibility that release of the substance could be linked' — and that no arrests have been made at this time. Assistant Chief Constable Tom Harding said that 'similar robberies have been reported at two European concerts' by the same artist, and that police would speak to European law enforcement to understand the wider picture. 'We maintain our belief that, based on the information available to us now, there is no wider ongoing risk to the public,' Harding said. The incident unfolded at around 10 p.m. on Sunday, November 22, near the end of Toliver's performance on the second leg of his Nitrous – Octane World Tour, when people in the crowd began suffering eye irritation, coughing, breathing difficulties and a burning sensation in the throat. Police declared a major incident at 22:25 GMT and more than 12,000 people were safely evacuated from the arena; the North West Ambulance Service assessed 88 people at the scene for symptoms believed to be linked to the exposure, while one person was taken to Manchester Royal Infirmary for further treatment. The substance was initially believed to be tear gas, but police later said its identity and origin had not been established, and officers are testing items recovered from the arena. Toliver, who had been due to perform at London's O2 Arena on Monday, postponed the concert to December 15, with promoters citing production delays because his stage equipment remained at Co-op Live; Manchester ticketholders will receive automatic refunds. Writing on Instagram, Toliver sent his 'heart and prayers' to those injured, adding: 'Stop bringing bulls*** into my shows. It ain't cool.' Some concertgoers criticised venue security, saying searches were minimal, and Co-op Live said its priority remains visitor safety and it is working closely with police to identify the cause.

articles.title: The Chicks and Willie Colón join AI music lawsuit against Suno: 'Misappropriated identities'
articles.description: The Chicks and the estates of salsa bandleader Willie Colón and Sam & Dave singer Sam Moore have joined Jason Isbell's proposed class-action lawsuit against AI music generator Suno, in an amended complaint filed in Boston federal court on Tuesday, November 24. The amended complaint adds 16 new plaintiffs, bringing the total to 20, and accuses Suno of encoding musicians' identities into its AI models and answering their names with songs, text and cover images that evoke them, without consent. Suno said the claims are 'without merit' and that it will defend itself in court.
articles.body: The Chicks, the estates of Willie Colón and Sam Moore, and a slew of other artists have joined the legal fight against AI music generator Suno, in an amended complaint filed in Boston federal court on Tuesday, November 24. The amended complaint adds 16 new plaintiffs to the proposed class action first filed on August 31 by Jason Isbell, David Lowery, Guy Forsyth and Eduardo Calle, bringing the total to 20. Those joining include The Chicks — Martie Maguire, Natalie Maines and Emily Strayer — Dirty Projectors founder David Longstreth, Detroit techno producer Carl Craig, Mount Eerie's Phil Elverum and singer-songwriter Ezra Furman, plus Andrew Choi (St. Lenox), Lydia Loveless, Laurel Massé, Franz Nicolay, William Pollak (Billy Price), Kealiʻi Reichel and Ike Reilly. The surviving spouses of salsa bandleader Willie Colón, who died in February 2026, and Sam & Dave singer Sam Moore, who died in January 2025, have signed on too. The Chicks, who have a long history of outspoken advocacy, represent by far the biggest living musical act yet to sue over AI. The case contains no copyright claims. Instead, it accuses Suno of encoding musicians' identities into its AI models and answering their names with songs, text descriptions and cover images that evoke them, without consent, under right-of-publicity laws in 14 US states and Puerto Rico, as well as Illinois' Biometric Information Privacy Act. The amended filing also adds demonstrations using Suno's v6 models, which launched in September, after the original suit was filed: it says every musician featured in the original filing's demonstrations was also run through v6, and that 'The Chicks and each band member's name are separately still accepted as prompts in Suno and produce outputs similar to prior outputs'. It also says entering 'Willie Colon' without the accent returned salsa tracks Suno repeatedly labelled 'trombone-led', and that several of the songs were named after him and included his name in the lyrics with the proper accent mark. The amended complaint comes 21 days after Suno asked the court to dismiss the case, arguing that using an artist's name in an AI text prompt is 'universal shorthand' for describing a musical style. In a statement to Billboard on Wednesday, November 25, a spokeswoman for Suno said the company believes 'these claims are without merit' and would defend itself in court: 'Suno exists to help people create new, original music, not to trade on anyone's name, and we prohibit any unauthorized use of an artist's work.' Isbell's lawsuit argues those safeguards can be easily duped, for example by typing names with spaces between the letters. The case is separate from the copyright lawsuits the major labels have brought against Suno, and its focus on identity rather than training data makes it a novel test of artists' likeness rights in the age of generative AI.

articles.title: UPDATE: Putin fires arrested Murmansk governor Chibis; court jails him until January 2027
articles.description: Vladimir Putin has dismissed Murmansk governor Andrei Chibis, days after he was detained in Moscow on corruption charges. On November 25 a Moscow court remanded Chibis in custody until January 23, 2027, over the alleged embezzlement of more than 1 billion rubles. The Kremlin said Putin was told in advance about the arrest.
articles.body: Vladimir Putin signed a decree on November 24 dismissing Andrei Chibis as governor of the Murmansk region, with the document published on November 25. Chibis was detained in Moscow on the evening of November 23, and on November 25 the Meshchansky District Court in Moscow remanded him in custody for two months, until January 23, 2027. Investigators accuse him of embezzling more than 1 billion rubles allocated for the reconstruction of the Apatity-Kirovsk road, stealing more than 39 million rubles from the regional construction ministry's budget, and conducting illegal currency operations. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Putin had been informed in advance that the governor would be detained. Chibis had run the Murmansk region for more than seven years and was long seen as a Kremlin loyalist, which makes his fall a striking example of how even senior regional leaders are not safe from corruption purges. Deputy governor Nadezhda Aksyonova will serve as acting head of the region. The case is one of the biggest corruption scandals involving a sitting governor in recent years, and it comes as the Kremlin continues to use high-profile arrests to signal discipline among regional elites.

articles.title: Roskomnadzor finds 'signs of extremism' in three Sobchak interviews; she deletes them
articles.description: Russia's media regulator Roskomnadzor has found 'signs of extremism' in three of Ksenia Sobchak's interviews and demanded their removal from YouTube. Sobchak deleted the episodes, which featured bloggers Hilmi and Igor Sinyak and singer Andrei Grigoryev-Appolonov. She called the demand 'a disgrace, of course, but what can you do'.
articles.body: Russia's media regulator Roskomnadzor has found 'signs of extremism' in three episodes of Ksenia Sobchak's show and demanded they be removed from YouTube, Meduza reported on November 25. The targeted interviews featured bloggers Hilmi, Igor Sinyak and singer Andrei Grigoryev-Appolonov. Sobchak deleted the episodes and commented: 'A disgrace, of course, but what can you do.' Sobchak, one of Russia's best-known media figures and a former presidential candidate, has walked a careful line since the full-scale invasion — remaining in Russia and on air while avoiding direct criticism of the war that would trigger prosecution. The regulator's move shows that even loyal, high-profile figures are not immune: Roskomnadzor has steadily expanded its use of 'extremism' findings to force the removal of interviews and commentary it dislikes. For Russia's remaining independent-minded broadcasters, the episode is a reminder that the space for interviews with outspoken guests keeps narrowing, and that self-censorship is now enforced by the threat of criminal liability.

articles.title: State Duma bans exam-free university admission for Olympiad winners
articles.description: Russia's State Duma has voted to end exam-free university admission for school Olympiad winners, with 424 deputies backing the change. Winners will still be credited with 100 points on the Unified State Exam in their subject, but the automatic route into university is gone. The reform ends a long-standing perk for talented school students.
articles.body: Russia's State Duma has adopted amendments abolishing admission to universities without entrance exams for winners of school Olympiads, Meduza reported on November 25. The law was supported by 424 deputies. Olympiad winners will keep the right to be treated as applicants who scored 100 points on the Unified State Exam in the subject matching their Olympiad profile, but the automatic, exam-free route into university is gone. The change ends a long-standing perk that made Olympiad victories a direct ticket into Russia's most prestigious universities, and it will reshape how ambitious school students plan their final years. Supporters of the reform argue the system was gamed by coaching and inflated results; critics say it punishes talented students from outside Moscow and St Petersburg, for whom Olympiads were one of the few ways to compete with well-connected applicants. The vote is part of a broader tightening of education rules in Russia, where the state has been steadily increasing control over universities, curricula and admissions.

articles.title: UPDATE: Kremlin calls Lukashenko's offer to fly Zelensky to Moscow 'very good' for him; Lukashenko urges a ceasefire
articles.description: The Kremlin has called Alexander Lukashenko's offer to fly to Moscow together with Volodymyr Zelensky 'very good' for the Ukrainian president, Meduza reported. Lukashenko separately urged Russia and Ukraine to agree a ceasefire. Zelensky had already dismissed the proposal as 'not a serious conversation', joking: 'What am I, his suitcase?'
articles.body: The Kremlin has welcomed Alexander Lukashenko's offer to fly to Moscow together with Volodymyr Zelensky for peace talks, calling it 'very good' for the Ukrainian president, Meduza reported on November 25. Lukashenko separately called on Russia and Ukraine to agree a ceasefire, in comments carried by Russian media. The Belarusian leader made the original offer in an interview with the French magazine Le Point, saying he could get on a plane with Zelensky and fly to Moscow as the guarantor of his security, and arguing that Russia, Ukraine and Belarus could reach a deal faster among themselves than with the Europeans. Zelensky dismissed the idea on Tuesday as 'not a serious conversation', joking: 'What am I, his suitcase?' and inviting Lukashenko and Putin to come to Kyiv instead. Putin has repeatedly said he would meet Zelensky only in Moscow — an offer Kyiv has rejected every time. The Kremlin's endorsement of Lukashenko's proposal shows Moscow is happy to keep the venue question in the headlines, even as the substance of any deal remains far off. It also underlines that the peace-talk debate is still stuck on the most basic question — where the two leaders could even meet.

articles.title: Nine Ukrainian children taken to Russia return home to their families
articles.description: Nine more Ukrainian children who had been taken to Russia have been reunited with their families, First Lady Melania Trump announced on November 25. Five of the children had been living with relatives in Russia and four in children's institutions. The returns came through her humanitarian initiative, one of the few working channels for bringing deported children home.
articles.body: Nine more Ukrainian children who had been taken to Russia have been reunited with their families, US First Lady Melania Trump announced on the White House website on Wednesday, November 25. Five of the children had been living in Russia with relatives, and four were in children's institutions, according to Russian children's ombudsman Maria Lvova-Belova. The returns took place under Melania Trump's humanitarian initiative, which has become one of the few working channels for bringing deported Ukrainian children home. Ukraine says Russia has deported or forcibly transferred tens of thousands of children since the full-scale invasion — a practice the International Criminal Court cited when it issued arrest warrants for Vladimir Putin and Lvova-Belova in 2023. Each return is negotiated individually and often takes months, involving mediators, paperwork and cross-border travel through third countries. While nine children is a small number against the scale of the deportations, every reunion matters to the families involved, and the initiative's continued operation shows that at least one humanitarian channel between the warring sides is still functioning.

articles.title: UPDATE: Chechen authorities deny Kadyrov's son received Serbian citizenship — but don't refute the evidence
articles.description: Chechen authorities have denied reports that Ali Kadyrov, son of Chechen leader Ramzan Kadyrov, received Serbian citizenship, calling them 'fake'. But as Meduza notes, officials did not refute the specific evidence cited in the investigation by the Anti-Corruption Foundation. The original report raised questions about why a member of the Kadyrov family would seek a second passport.
articles.body: Chechen authorities have denied reports that Ali Kadyrov, the son of Chechen leader Ramzan Kadyrov, received Serbian citizenship — but they have not refuted the evidence behind the claim, Meduza reported on November 25. Chechen vice-premier and minister for national policy Ilman Vakhidov called the reports 'fake', while failing to address the specific documents cited by the authors of the investigation, the Anti-Corruption Foundation (FBK). The original report said Ali Kadyrov had been granted Serbian citizenship, raising questions about why the son of one of Russia's most powerful regional leaders would seek a second passport — and what it might be used for. Serbian citizenship would give a member of the Kadyrov family visa-free travel across much of Europe and a potential safe haven outside Russia. Grozny's non-denial denial follows a familiar pattern: officials dismiss the story in general terms without engaging with the documents. The episode is a reminder of how the Kadyrov family's wealth and foreign ties remain a sensitive subject in Chechnya, where criticism of the leadership is effectively impossible.

articles.title: Ukraine's military intelligence destroys unique Russian aerospace reconnaissance complex in Smolensk region
articles.description: Ukraine's military intelligence has destroyed a unique Russian aerospace reconnaissance complex in the Smolensk region, Ukrainian media reported. The system could detect air targets up to 2,500 kilometres away, making it a key part of Russia's early-warning network. Its loss further weakens Russian air defences deep inside the country.
articles.body: Drone operators from Ukraine's military intelligence (GUR) have destroyed a unique Russian aerospace reconnaissance complex in the Smolensk region, Ukrainian media reported on November 25. The system was capable of detecting air targets at a distance of up to 2,500 kilometres, making it a key node in Russia's early-warning and air-defence network. Losing it blinds Russian air defences across a wide area and makes it harder for Moscow to track Ukrainian long-range drones and missiles heading for targets deep inside Russia. The strike fits the pattern of Ukraine's recent deep-strike campaign, which has hit refineries in the Samara region and warplanes at the Savasleyka airbase in the space of a single night. GUR has specialised in precisely this kind of operation — small, hard-to-detect drone teams striking high-value, hard-to-replace military infrastructure far from the front. Such systems take years to build and cannot be quickly replaced, so each successful strike degrades Russia's ability to defend its own airspace a little further.

articles.title: UPDATE: Russia's overnight mass strike on Ukraine's energy grid hits four regions; a DTEK power plant stops working
articles.description: Russia again massively struck Ukraine's energy infrastructure overnight, damaging substations, power lines and gas facilities in four regions, Prime Minister Koretskyi said. One DTEK thermal power plant stopped working, and large parts of Zaporizhzhia lost power and water. A morning strike on the city injured six more people, including two children, after the previous day's attacks killed two and injured 50.
articles.body: Russia again launched a mass strike on Ukraine's energy infrastructure overnight on November 25, Prime Minister Koretskyi said, with damage to substations, generating facilities, power lines and gas infrastructure in the Zaporizhzhia, Odesa, Dnipropetrovsk and Poltava regions. One thermal power plant operated by DTEK stopped working after the attack. Large parts of Zaporizhzhia were left without electricity, electric transport stopped in the regional centre, residents reported interruptions to the water supply, and traffic across the Dnipro hydroelectric dam was closed. Earlier, a morning strike on Zaporizhzhia's Shevchenkivskyi district injured six people, including two children, adding to the toll from the previous day's attacks, which killed two people and injured 50. Russia also claimed strikes on the Kryvyi Rih thermal power plant, substations in Zaporizhzhia and Zelenodolsk, railway locomotives in Dnipro, an industrial facility in Chernihiv region and a cargo ship in the port of Chornomorsk. Ukraine's air defences shot down or suppressed 88 of the 112 drones launched overnight, including 66 jet-powered Shaheds. The attacks continue Russia's autumn campaign against Ukrainian energy infrastructure, which has left parts of the country on hourly power outages as winter sets in.

articles.title: UPDATE: SAP chief says SBU may have been preparing to detain NABU director during 'Carthage' operation
articles.description: SAP chief Oleksandr Klymenko has told Ukraїnska Pravda that SBU special forces may have been preparing to detain NABU director Semen Kryvonos in September, after the first stage of the 'Carthage' anti-corruption operation. Two buses of special forces were stationed by the NABU building, and their presence was documented. Klymenko said he has no information about the President's Office being involved.
articles.body: The head of the Specialised Anti-Corruption Prosecutor's Office (SAP), Oleksandr Klymenko, has said the Security Service of Ukraine (SBU) may have been preparing to detain the director of the National Anti-Corruption Bureau (NABU), Semen Kryvonos, Ukraїnska Pravda reported. In an interview published on November 24, Klymenko said that in September 2026, after the first stage of the anti-corruption operation 'Carthage', SBU special-forces buses were stationed by the NABU building. NABU's internal control unit documented their presence and established they belonged to the SBU, though it could not identify the specific unit. Klymenko linked the incident to a claim by then-prosecutor general Ruslan Kravchenko about a supposed suspicion against the NABU director, and suggested the detention may not have happened because Kravchenko went abroad. He acknowledged he does not know the special forces' exact task or who ordered them to the building, and said he has no information about the involvement of the President's Office. The claim adds a new twist to the confrontation between Ukraine's anti-corruption bodies and parts of the security services, which escalated after the second stage of 'Carthage' began on November 4, with SBU Major-General Serhiy Duka among the suspects. For Ukraine's Western partners, the independence of NABU and SAP is a key condition for continued support and EU accession, so the standoff is being watched closely in Brussels and Washington.

articles.title: Ukraine to speed up implementation of agreements with Hungary on minority rights
articles.description: Ukraine and Hungary have discussed speeding up implementation of their agreements on protecting national minority rights, Ukraїnska Pravda reported. The move follows Prime Minister Péter Magyar's visit to Zakarpattia, where he and President Zelenskyy agreed on 10 points on Hungarian minority rights plus concrete deals on gas, diesel, border crossings and direct trains.
articles.body: Ukraine and Hungary have discussed speeding up the implementation of their agreements on protecting the rights of national minorities, Ukraїnska Pravda reported on November 25. The discussion follows Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar's visit to Zakarpattia region, where he held talks with President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and the two sides agreed on 10 points concerning the rights of the Hungarian minority. Zelenskyy also reported 'concrete agreements' on gas and diesel supplies, border crossing points and direct train services between the two countries. The minority-rights question has been one of the most sensitive issues in Ukrainian-Hungarian relations: Budapest has long pressed Kyiv over the rights of ethnic Hungarians in Zakarpattia, particularly on education in the Hungarian language, and has at times used the issue to block Ukraine's progress towards the EU and NATO. The agreement — and now the push to implement it faster — suggests both sides want to remove an irritant that Russia has repeatedly tried to exploit. For Kyiv, settling the dispute matters because Hungary's veto power inside the EU makes Budapest's goodwill valuable as accession talks proceed.

articles.title: Verkhovna Rada backs Ukraine joining steering committee of Special Tribunal on Russian aggression
articles.description: Ukraine's parliament has backed the country's accession to the Steering Committee of the Special Tribunal for the crime of aggression against Ukraine. The tribunal, being set up under the Council of Europe, is meant to prosecute Russia's leadership for launching the full-scale invasion. Joining the committee gives Kyiv a formal say in how it is built and run.
articles.body: Ukraine's parliament, the Verkhovna Rada, has supported Ukraine's accession to the Steering Committee of the Special Tribunal for the crime of aggression against Ukraine, Ukrainian media reported on November 25. The decision was part of a package of measures adopted by MPs on the day, which also included the law legalising the cryptocurrency market, a step towards separating electricity generation from the activities of the gas transmission system operator, and measures to preserve state-owned coal-mining and uranium-mining enterprises. The Special Tribunal, being set up under the auspices of the Council of Europe, is intended to prosecute Russia's leadership for the crime of aggression — the decision to launch the full-scale invasion — which falls outside the jurisdiction of the International Criminal Court. Joining its steering committee gives Kyiv a formal say in how the tribunal is built and run, including its rules, staffing and funding. For Ukraine, the tribunal is a long-term project: even if prosecutions take years, it is meant to ensure that the decision to start the war does not go unpunished, and to create a legal record of Russian aggression for history.

articles.title: Ukraine's Blysk laser shoots down a jet-powered Shahed — a world first
articles.description: Ukraine's Blysk laser air-defence system has shot down a Russian jet-powered Shahed drone, presidential adviser Serhii 'Flash' Beskrestnov said on November 25 — the first time in the world a combat laser has destroyed a jet-powered strike drone. The 4-kilowatt system, built by Carmine Sky, has been on combat duty in Kyiv since early November. Beskrestnov published video of the engagement.
articles.body: Ukraine's Blysk laser air-defence system has shot down a Russian jet-powered Shahed drone — the first time in the world a combat laser has destroyed a jet-powered strike drone, presidential adviser Serhii 'Flash' Beskrestnov said on November 25. The laser, developed by the private Ukrainian company Carmine Sky, was guarding a critical infrastructure site when it destroyed a jet-powered Geran drone, Beskrestnov said, publishing a 21-second video of the engagement. The footage shows the operator's screen locking onto the target at a range of about 730 metres and a height of around 400 metres, before the drone goes down in a cloud of smoke. Blysk fires a 4-kilowatt beam with a range of about one kilometre, burning through a drone's hull in a matter of seconds; it has been on combat duty in Kyiv since the start of November. The system was developed under the state's 'Private Air Defence' programme with support from the Brave1 defence-tech cluster. Beskrestnov cautioned that it is still too early to talk about serial production, with testing continuing while the lasers protect critical sites. If the claim holds up, it marks a milestone for laser weapons — a cheap way to defeat drones that cost far more to shoot down with missiles — and a significant boost for Ukraine's air defences, which face nightly waves of Shaheds, including 66 jet-powered ones in the night to November 25 alone.

articles.title: Nvidia cuts production of RTX 50 graphics cards by up to a third as AI chips take priority
articles.description: Nvidia has decided to cut shipments of its GeForce RTX 50 series graphics cards by 20–30%, according to Commercial Times, citing Taiwanese supply-chain partners. The cuts are already under way and will tighten availability of the gaming GPUs. The move reflects Nvidia shifting wafer capacity toward far more profitable AI data-centre chips.
articles.body: Nvidia has decided to reduce production of its GeForce RTX 50 series graphics cards by 20–30%, Commercial Times reports, citing Taiwanese partners in the company's supply chain. The cuts have already begun, and volumes will shrink in the coming months, meaning the RTX 50 cards — the current generation of Nvidia gaming GPUs — are about to become harder to find and potentially more expensive. The decision comes as demand for AI accelerators continues to dwarf gaming demand: Nvidia earns far more per wafer from data-centre chips than from consumer graphics cards, so fab capacity is being redirected there. For PC gamers the timing is awkward, with the holiday season approaching and RTX 50 cards already selling at a premium in many markets. It also underlines how the AI boom is reshaping the consumer hardware market — the same silicon shortage logic that has pushed up memory and component prices is now hitting graphics cards directly. Rival AMD could benefit if it can keep its own cards in stock, but the whole GPU market tends to move together on supply. Anyone planning a PC upgrade may want to buy sooner rather than later, before the reduced shipments feed through to retail prices.

articles.title: Team Cherry to hold Hollow Knight presentation on November 27 with news on Silksong's Sea of Sorrow expansion
articles.description: Australian studio Team Cherry has announced a special presentation, Cherry Time, for November 27 at 18:00 Moscow time. The developers promise fresh details on Sea of Sorrow, the large free expansion for Hollow Knight: Silksong, as well as other announcements. It is the first dedicated showcase for the expansion since Silksong's launch.
articles.body: Team Cherry, the Australian studio behind Hollow Knight, has announced a special presentation called Cherry Time, scheduled for November 27 at 18:00 Moscow time. The developers promise to share fresh details about Sea of Sorrow, the major free expansion for Hollow Knight: Silksong, along with further announcements. Sea of Sorrow is the first big content addition to Silksong, the long-awaited sequel that finally launched after years of anticipation and became one of the biggest indie releases in recent memory. Little has been officially revealed about the expansion so far, so the presentation is the first real look at what it adds — new areas, bosses and abilities are the obvious hopes, given the original Hollow Knight's own expansions set a high bar. The showcase format is a notable step for Team Cherry, a tiny team that has historically communicated sparingly and let its games speak for themselves. For Silksong players, the date is now circled: a free expansion to one of the year's defining games, shown off in a dedicated broadcast rather than buried in a larger event.

articles.title: Digital Foundry: GTA VI runs better on Xbox Series X than on PlayStation 5
articles.description: Digital Foundry has compared Grand Theft Auto VI on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and concluded that Microsoft's console handles the game better, holding a more stable frame rate. The finding is striking given that the PS5 version drove the game's record-breaking launch. Both versions remain strong, but the Xbox edges it on performance consistency.
articles.body: Digital Foundry has put Grand Theft Auto VI through its paces on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X, and its verdict is that Microsoft's console runs the game better than Sony's. The Xbox Series X holds a more stable frame rate, which is especially notable because the PlayStation 5 version was the one behind the game's record-shattering launch — more than 39 million players on PS5 in the first four days, the biggest PlayStation launch ever. The analysis looked at how each console copes with the game's dense open world of Leonida, where frame-rate dips are most likely in busy city scenes and during heavy action. Both versions are still impressive technical achievements, and the differences are the kind that matter most to players sensitive to smooth performance rather than to casual players. The result also feeds the long-running console rivalry in an unusual way: Rockstar's biggest game ever, on the platform where it sold most, runs slightly better on the rival machine. Rockstar has already released its first patch for the game, fixing crashes and weather and wanted-level bugs, and further optimisation updates are expected. For now, the performance crown sits with Xbox — a talking point that will run for a while.

articles.title: Nioh 3 comes to Xbox for the first time as Koei Tecmo announces Complete Edition
articles.description: Koei Tecmo has announced Nioh 3: Complete Edition, bringing Team Ninja's dark samurai action RPG to Xbox for the first time in the series' history. The edition bundles the base game with its two paid story expansions, the second of which, Bloody Insurrection, arrives December 17. The Complete Edition launches January 28, 2027 on Xbox Series X|S, PlayStation 5 and PC.
articles.body: Koei Tecmo has announced Nioh 3: Complete Edition, a package that bundles the base game with its two paid story expansions — and, for the first time in the series' history, brings Nioh to Xbox. The Complete Edition launches January 28, 2027 on Xbox Series X|S, PlayStation 5 and PC. The second expansion, Bloody Insurrection, arrives December 17 and adds the new Shimabara region, wrapping up the conspiracy from the first expansion, with Amakusa Shiro, Tachibana Muneshige and other figures joining the cast, plus new yokai, guardian spirits and endgame content in the form of the Shura Battlefield. Both expansions also open a fourth playthrough cycle and a new top equipment rarity. Nioh has been a PlayStation-associated series since the original launched as a PS4 exclusive in 2017, so its arrival on Xbox marks a real shift in Koei Tecmo's platform strategy — following a wider industry trend of former exclusives going multiplatform. For Xbox players, it means the full Nioh 3 experience, including both expansions, in a single package. For existing players, the December DLC is the more immediate date: a new region and a new endgame grind just before the holidays.

articles.title: Rockstar is open to a Red Dead Redemption film or TV adaptation
articles.description: Rockstar Games is ready to consider offers for a film or television adaptation of Red Dead Redemption, according to The Ankler journalist Lesley Goldberg. The studio has discussed a possible deal in the past without reaching one. No project is agreed yet, but the door is now open for one of gaming's most cinematic stories to reach the screen.
articles.body: Rockstar Games is open to a film or television adaptation of Red Dead Redemption, according to The Ankler journalist Lesley Goldberg, citing people familiar with the matter. The studio is prepared to consider offers to bring its western saga to the screen, and possible deals have been discussed before without coming to anything. No agreement is in place, and there is no word yet on whether it would be a film or a series, or which studio might take it on. The news matters because Red Dead Redemption — particularly its 2018 prequel, Red Dead Redemption 2 — is widely regarded as one of the most cinematic games ever made, with a story of loyalty, betrayal and the dying Old West that many critics have compared favourably with prestige television. Rockstar has historically been extremely protective of its properties and has resisted Hollywood adaptations, unlike many of its rivals, which makes even a willingness to listen significant. The success of recent game adaptations, from The Last of Us to Fallout, has shown studios that faithful, big-budget versions of beloved games can work. If a deal happens, the casting of Arthur Morgan alone would become one of the most debated choices in entertainment.

articles.title: CD Projekt promises a GTA VI-scale leap for The Witcher 4 and signs PlayStation marketing deal
articles.description: CD Projekt RED says The Witcher 4 aims for a leap over The Witcher 3 comparable to the jump Rockstar made from GTA V to GTA VI, co-CEO Michał Nowakowski told The Game Business. The studio has also signed a deal with Sony Interactive Entertainment, which will take part in marketing the game. A boxed edition is confirmed, though whether it will include a disc is still unclear.
articles.body: CD Projekt RED has set an enormous bar for The Witcher 4: the developers aim to make a leap over The Witcher 3 comparable to the one Rockstar Games achieved going from Grand Theft Auto V to Grand Theft Auto VI, co-CEO Michał Nowakowski said in an interview with The Game Business. It is a bold comparison, given that GTA VI has just posted the biggest launch in entertainment history, but it signals how confident the Polish studio is about its next chapter — a new saga starring Ciri rather than Geralt. Separately, CD Projekt has signed an agreement with Sony Interactive Entertainment under which PlayStation will take part in marketing The Witcher 4, a partnership that suggests Sony sees the game as a flagship title for its platform. Nowakowski also confirmed the game will get a boxed retail edition, though he said it is not yet clear whether a disc will be included — a sign of how far the industry has drifted toward digital even for major releases. The Witcher 3, released in 2015, remains one of the most acclaimed RPGs ever made, so matching its legacy, let alone leaping past it, is a formidable task. No release date has been announced, but the marketing deal and the confident talk suggest the project is entering a more public phase.

articles.title: Samsung unveils the world's first 1100 Hz gaming monitor
articles.description: Samsung Electronics has unveiled the 27-inch Odyssey G6 (G60H), a gaming monitor with a refresh rate of up to 1100 Hz — the first display in the world to reach that speed. The monitor is aimed squarely at competitive gamers, where even tiny gains in smoothness and response time matter. No price or release date has been announced yet.
articles.body: Samsung Electronics has presented the world's first gaming monitor with a refresh rate of 1100 Hz: the 27-inch Odyssey G6 (G60H). The display can refresh its image up to 1,100 times per second, far beyond the 240 Hz or 360 Hz panels that are currently considered fast, and even beyond the 500–600 Hz monitors that have only recently started appearing. The monitor is aimed first and foremost at competitive gamers, where higher refresh rates mean smoother motion and a fractionally faster view of the action — an edge that matters in esports titles like Counter-Strike 2 and Valorant, even if the difference is invisible to most casual players. Driving 1100 frames per second will, of course, require an extremely powerful PC, and only a handful of games can reach those frame rates even on top-end hardware. Samsung has not yet announced pricing or a release date. The launch is still significant as a marker of where display technology is heading: refresh rates that once seemed absurd are becoming a competitive battleground, and Samsung is now leading it. For most players, a 144 Hz or 240 Hz screen remains more than enough — but the ceiling has just moved dramatically.

articles.title: At least 30 killed in fuel tanker fire near Cairo, Egypt's Health Ministry says
articles.description: A tanker truck carrying petroleum products crashed in Egypt's Giza governorate on Wednesday, igniting a massive fire that killed at least 30 people and injured 19 others, according to the Egyptian Ministry of Health and Population. The fire broke out above Tunnel 10 in the Warraq district of Imbaba, near Cairo's Ring Road. It is a developing story.
articles.body: At least 30 people have been killed and 19 injured after a tanker truck carrying petroleum products crashed and caught fire in Egypt's Giza governorate on Wednesday, the Egyptian Ministry of Health and Population said. The fire broke out above Tunnel 10 in the Warraq district of Imbaba, near Cairo's Ring Road, one of the capital's busiest routes. The crash ignited the tanker's load, producing a huge blaze that emergency services fought to bring under control. Details of what caused the tanker to crash remain unclear, and the ministry said the casualty figures could change as rescue work continues. Fuel tanker crashes are a recurring hazard on Egypt's crowded roads, where heavy trucks share highways with dense traffic and safety enforcement is patchy. The Warraq district sits on the western edge of Cairo, a sprawling urban area where the Ring Road carries a constant stream of freight. CNN described the story as developing, with updates expected as more information emerges from Egyptian authorities. For Cairo, a city where traffic accidents already claim many lives each year, the scale of the toll — 30 dead in a single incident — makes it one of the deadliest road disasters in the country this year.

articles.title: Netanyahu gets major legal boost as court casts doubt on corruption case
articles.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's years-long corruption trial took a significant turn in his favour on Wednesday, as judges recommended prosecutors drop charges in the most serious of the three cases against him and reconsider a second. Netanyahu called the recommendation a vindication and declared: 'This trial needs to end immediately.' The judges' view is not binding, but it is a major boost for Israel's longest-serving leader.
articles.body: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's years-long corruption trial took a significant turn in his favour on Wednesday, as judges recommended that prosecutors drop the charges in the most serious of the three cases against him and reconsider a second case. Judge Rivka Friedman-Feldman, who is presiding over the trial, indicated to Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara in a hearing that a conviction of Netanyahu in what is known as Case 4000 is unlikely and the case should be dropped. Case 4000 alleges Netanyahu granted regulatory favours to the telecoms giant Bezeq in exchange for favourable coverage on its Walla news site — the most serious of the three cases, which also include charges of fraud, breach of trust and bribery. In televised remarks later on Wednesday, Netanyahu said the recommendations amount to a vindication and declared: 'This trial needs to end immediately.' He also repeated that he is prepared to form a unity government with the parliamentary opposition. His political rival Gadi Eisenkot is meanwhile manoeuvring to form a government that would oust Netanyahu and his far-right partners after nearly four years in power. The judges' recommendation is not binding on prosecutors, who must still decide whether to follow it, but the signal from the bench carries enormous weight in a trial that has dominated Israeli politics for years. If Case 4000 is dropped, it would remove the most damaging charge hanging over Netanyahu and reshape the political landscape as coalition talks continue.

articles.title: UPDATE: Vance says he was told Jensen Huang was not under investigation
articles.description: Vice President JD Vance said Wednesday that federal officials told him reinstated Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was not under investigation, downplaying concerns that Huang's reported affair with a woman suspected of having ties to Chinese intelligence could pose a national security risk. 'We were told that he was under no investigation,' Vance told CNN's Kit Maher at a pre-Thanksgiving meal for US troops in Dayton, Ohio.
articles.body: Vice President JD Vance said on Wednesday that federal officials told him reinstated Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was not under investigation, moving to downplay concerns that Huang's reported affair with a woman suspected of having ties to Chinese intelligence could pose a national security risk. 'We were told that he was under no investigation,' Vance told CNN's Kit Maher at a pre-Thanksgiving meal for US troops in Dayton, Ohio. The comment is the administration's latest attempt to close the book on the extraordinary saga that saw Huang ousted as Nvidia CEO and then reinstated just 11 days later, after President Trump personally pushed the board to bring him back. Huang apologised to employees and said he was in therapy at his first meeting since his return, and the company's board — several of whose members have served for three decades — has faced sharp criticism over its handling of the affair, with one prominent governance expert calling the reinstatement 'a complete failure of corporate governance'. Trump has openly taken credit for the reinstatement, despite bipartisan concerns about whether China is using advanced Nvidia chips to bolster its military capabilities by bypassing export restrictions. Vance's assurance does not settle the underlying questions: US officials had feared the woman could be a Chinese intelligence asset, and lawmakers from both parties have raised concerns about the episode. But it signals the White House wants the matter treated as closed — even as the board's independence and the company's governance remain under scrutiny.

articles.title: New images reveal stadium-size crater left by humanity's first planetary defence test
articles.description: The European Space Agency's Hera spacecraft has arrived at the asteroid Dimorphos and released its first images, revealing a stadium-size crater left by NASA's DART impact four years ago. The crater flattened one of the asteroid's previously rounded faces, and scientists were surprised to find hundreds of previously unknown boulders encircling the asteroid pair. The findings will shape how humanity might one day deflect a dangerous asteroid.
articles.body: NASA's DART spacecraft moved an asteroid called Dimorphos four years ago in humanity's first planetary defence test — a mission to explore whether it is possible to stop an asteroid from hitting Earth. Now scientists are getting a closer look at the result. The European Space Agency's Hera spacecraft, which launched in October 2024, arrived at Dimorphos three weeks ago and is currently about 30 kilometres (19 miles) from the space rock, which orbits a larger asteroid named Didymos in what is known as a binary asteroid system. The ESA released the mission's first images on Wednesday, and they show a stadium-size crater that flattened one of the asteroid's previously rounded faces — the scar left when DART slammed into the rock at 13,645 miles per hour. The biggest surprise from Hera's early observations is that hundreds of previously unknown boulders encircle the asteroid pair, including more than 100 that are between the size of a football and a washing machine, according to Naomi Murdoch, a planetary scientist at the University of Toulouse who is part of the mission team. Scientists had expected the impact to scatter debris, but the scale and distribution of the boulders is new information. The data matters because planetary defence depends on knowing exactly how an asteroid responds to being hit: if humanity ever needs to deflect a genuinely dangerous object, the models must be right. Hera will spend months mapping Dimorphos in detail, measuring the crater and the debris field to refine those models.

articles.title: UPDATE: Thanksgiving storms now lashing both coasts as 81 million Americans travel
articles.description: The Thanksgiving storms are now hitting both US coasts, with more than 81 million people expected to travel for the holiday. The East Coast nor'easter is bringing flooding rain and strong winds, with streets already flooding in Hollywood, Florida, while California faces evacuation warnings and near-record king tides. The FAA expects the busiest Thanksgiving travel period in 16 years.
articles.body: The storms threatening Thanksgiving travel are now lashing both coasts of the United States, with more than 81 million people expected to travel for the holiday. On the East Coast, the nor'easter is strengthening as it tracks up the coast, bringing soaking rain, strong winds and severe coastal flooding, with rainfall rates of up to an inch per hour and gusts exceeding 50 mph along the coast. In Hollywood, Florida, streets were already flooding as the storm arrived, with residents filling sandbags and pumps working to clear standing water — an area still recovering from last week's historic flooding, when one resident said her four-bedroom house had five inches of water in every room. Rain is expected to reach New York City on Thanksgiving morning, with gusts over 40 mph posing problems for the 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade balloons — city rules require balloons to fly lower or stay grounded if sustained winds exceed 23 mph or gusts top 34 mph. On the West Coast, San Francisco Bay could rise to near-record levels, with water expected to reach 8.5 feet during Wednesday morning's high tide, inches shy of the 1983 record of 8.82 feet, and 20- to 30-foot waves are forecast at Ocean Beach. Parts of California are under evacuation warnings, with rain and wind expected across the state and the Pacific Northwest. The National Weather Service has issued a rare coastal flood warning for the San Francisco Bay area running through Thanksgiving Day, and the mayor has asked residents to consider not travelling unless essential. The FAA expects the busiest Thanksgiving travel period in 16 years, with more than 417,000 flights scheduled over nine days, and rain could disrupt flights from the Southeast to New York and as far west as Chicago.

articles.title: Beatles attraction at former Apple Corps HQ — site of the band's final public concert — approved by London council
articles.description: Westminster City Council has approved plans for a Beatles visitor attraction at 3 Savile Row, the former Apple Corps headquarters where the band played its final public concert on the rooftop in January 1969. The attraction, first unveiled in May as 'The Beatles at 3 Savile Row', will include exhibitions from the Apple Corps archives, a recreated basement studio and access to the rooftop, and is expected to open in 2027. Draft planning conditions reportedly include a ban on live music on the rooftop terrace.
articles.body: Westminster City Council's Planning Committee signed off on the plans on Tuesday, November 24, for a Beatles visitor attraction at 3 Savile Row, the former London headquarters of Apple Corps. The attraction, first unveiled in May under the name 'The Beatles at 3 Savile Row', will feature exhibitions drawn from the Apple Corps archives, a recreated version of the basement recording studio where the band worked on 'Let It Be' in 1969, and access to the rooftop where John Lennon, Paul McCartney, George Harrison and Ringo Starr — joined by Billy Preston — played their last public live performance on January 30, 1969. Apple Corps CEO Tom Greene told the committee the company wants to return the front of the building to how it looked and felt in 1969, 'right down to the Apple green carpet', supplemented with the latest AV technology for an immersive experience, and to host bookable evening events with a cafe and bar in the basement for ticket holders. According to the BBC, the planning papers expect as many as 900 visitors a day on weekdays and 1,140 on weekends, while the Savile Row Bespoke Association objected, warning the street's narrow sidewalks could become congested. Greene noted Apple Corps bought back the headlease after the building was sold in the mid-1970s, and pointed to a letter Paul McCartney sent the committee about how much the building means to him. The project is part of a wider Apple Corps expansion: in October it announced plans to take over The Beatles Story in Liverpool and move it to a 100,000-square-foot city-centre site in 2028, and Sam Mendes' four Beatles films are set for release in April 2028.

articles.title: Coachella sues Walmart for trademark infringement over unlicensed festival merch
articles.description: The companies behind Coachella have sued Walmart for trademark infringement, alleging the retailer has repeatedly sold merchandise bearing Coachella's trademarks without a licence despite demands dating back to 2017. The complaint, filed on November 24 in the US District Court for the Central District of California by Coachella Music Festival, LLC and promoter Goldenvoice, calls Walmart a 'serial infringer' and seeks an injunction, trebled damages and punitive damages. Walmart has more than 4,600 US locations and is described in the filing as 'the world's largest retailer'.
articles.body: The companies behind Coachella have sued Walmart for trademark infringement, alleging the retailer has repeatedly sold merchandise bearing Coachella's trademarks without a licence despite demands dating back to 2017. The complaint, obtained and first reported by MBW, was filed on Tuesday, November 24, in the US District Court for the Central District of California by Coachella Music Festival, LLC and Goldenvoice, LLC, the AEG-owned promoter behind the festival. It brings claims of trademark infringement and false designation of origin under the federal Lanham Act, plus unfair competition and misleading advertising claims under California law, asserting rights in 12 US trademark registrations covering marks including Coachella, Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival and 'Chella', as well as the festival's palm tree logo. One section of the filing is headed with the claim that Walmart is a 'serial infringer', listing intellectual property disputes stretching back to the late 1990s, including a $6.4 million settlement Walmart paid to resolve a Tommy Hilfiger lawsuit over counterfeit T-shirts, and claims brought by Nike, Yeti Coolers, Crocs, Vans and Deckers. The earliest incident detailed took place in June 2017, when Walmart advertised at least 28 apparel items displaying the Coachella mark on its website; further incidents followed, including apparel sold at its North Indio store in April 2019, a 2022 social-media post for its Dr. Thunder soft drink using a photo of Coachella's Ferris wheel, and signage at its La Quinta store in April 2023 copied from the festival's line-up posters. The complaint alleges that in April 2026, 'undeterred by knowledge at the highest corporate levels', Walmart resumed selling unlicensed Coachella products at the La Quinta store, using a point-of-sale Ferris wheel sign produced by festival sponsor Absolut Vodka, and cites Instagram videos from a Palm Springs news outlet showing Coachella-branded tumblers, bottles and tank tops at the North Indio Walmart under the caption 'Who needs the merch tent [at Coachella] when you have the North Indio Walmart?' The plaintiffs say Walmart 'typically stops for a period of time, but then resumes its infringing conduct', and are seeking a temporary restraining order, preliminary and permanent injunctions, damages trebled for alleged wilfulness, Walmart's profits from the infringement, corrective advertising costs, attorneys' fees and punitive damages under California law, with a jury trial demanded. The case is the latest in a wave of litigation over unlicensed merchandise, though most such cases have targeted anonymous sellers rather than a major retailer, and it reflects both merch's growing importance to artists' income and how easily knock-offs can now be produced and sold.

articles.title: Believe fully acquires Lili Louise Musique, parent of French indie tôt Ou tard, eight years after buying a 49% stake
articles.description: Believe has fully acquired Lili Louise Musique, the parent company of French label tôt Ou tard, becoming the group's sole shareholder. The Paris-headquartered company announced the deal on Wednesday, November 25, calling it 'a natural continuation' of a partnership that began in 2018, when Believe acquired a 49% stake. Founder Vincent Frèrebeau will continue to lead the group, which keeps its identity, teams and artistic autonomy.
articles.body: Believe has fully acquired Lili Louise Musique, the parent company of French label tôt Ou tard, becoming the group's sole shareholder, the Paris-headquartered company announced on Wednesday, November 25. Believe called the deal 'a natural continuation' of a partnership that began in 2018, when it acquired a 49% stake in Lili Louise Musique from Wagram Music — a stake its pre-IPO filings later showed cost €12.3 million. Founder Vincent Frèrebeau will continue to lead the group and will retain 'full control over [the group's] directions and artistic choices', with each brand under the umbrella keeping its identity, organisation, teams, premises and corporate culture. The deal covers all of Lili Louise Musique's activities, including tôt Ou tard, live performance company Zouave and publishing arm LLM, plus Guess What, a company dedicated to 'innovative projects', and the group's stakes in live music company Uni-t. 'Ever since I created tôt Ou tard, our obsession has been to give time to artists and their projects,' said Frèrebeau. 'Time to explore, create, develop, and ultimately meet their audience and build sustainable careers.' Believe's Global Head of Music Romain Vivien noted that tôt Ou tard, which celebrated its 30th anniversary this year, is one of the rare independent labels to last so long while racking up a series of artist-development successes. MBW described tôt Ou tard in 2018 as the second-biggest independent label in France, behind Because Music, with best-known signings then including French singer-songwriters Vianney and Vincent Delerm, as well as Shaka Ponk. Financial terms of the latest transaction were not disclosed. The deal follows Believe's move in October to expand Vivien's role, putting him in direct charge of the company's three geographic regions, and comes after the consortium led by founder Denis Ladegaillerie, the EQT X fund and TCV funds took Believe private, completing a squeeze-out of minority shareholders and delisting the company from Euronext Paris in August 2025. Believe operates in more than 50 countries and employs more than 2,000 people.

articles.title: Downtown Music Publishing appoints ex-Luminate exec Helena Kosinski and Armada's Michel Peek to new international roles
articles.description: Downtown Music Publishing has appointed Helena Kosinski as Senior Vice President of International Strategy and Business Development and Michel Peek, formerly of Armada Music, as General Manager of UK & Europe. The Virgin Music Group-owned publisher announced the two newly created roles on Wednesday, November 25, as part of a new international expansion strategy. Kosinski will drive DMP's international growth from London, while Peek leads its UK and European push from Virgin Music Group's Amsterdam offices.
articles.body: Downtown Music Publishing (DMP) has appointed Helena Kosinski as Senior Vice President of International Strategy and Business Development, and Michel Peek, formerly of Armada Music, as General Manager of UK & Europe, the Virgin Music Group-owned publisher announced on Wednesday, November 25. The two newly created roles form part of a new international expansion strategy. London-based Kosinski will 'lead the growth and transformation of the international business', including spotting growth opportunities globally, setting DMP's strategy for signing clients and songwriters, and developing partnerships and commercial opportunities; she will report directly to DMP President Emily Stephenson. Kosinski joins from her own consulting company, where she advised data and technology companies on the music business, and previously held executive positions at Luminate and its predecessors MRC Data and Nielsen Music, where she led the international business; Luminate powers the Billboard charts. She is also Chair of the Advisory Board at Music Technology UK. 'There is a huge opportunity for us to extend our offering to publishers, songwriters, artists and other partners around the world by leveraging the full strength of our publishing platform,' Kosinski said. Peek, based in Virgin Music Group's Amsterdam offices, is tasked with growing DMP's presence in the UK and Europe, building relationships with independent publishers, labels, managers and collecting societies, and developing publishing partnerships; he will report to Kosinski. He joins from Armada Music, where he set up the company's publishing arm in 2018 and served as General Manager of Armada Music Publishing. The appointments come nine months after Universal Music Group's Virgin Music Group completed its $775 million acquisition of Downtown Music Holdings on February 20, bringing DMP, Songtrust, FUGA, CD Baby and Downtown Artist & Label Services under its ownership. DMP's existing international operations include Downtown Music Publishing Africa, launched in May 2025, and the company says its clients and songwriters earned 44 nominations at the 2026 Grammy Awards, including for Album of the Year (Bad Bunny), and won 11 awards at the 2025 Latin Grammys. DMP says it represents the catalogues of John Lennon, Atticus Ross and Phish, and in May struck a deal to represent the catalogue of Biz Markie, as well as the late artist's name, image and likeness rights.

articles.title: Musixmatch launches enhanced Pro for Artists platform with lyric merch, fan analytics and 'optional AI licensing coming soon'
articles.description: Musixmatch has launched a new version of its Musixmatch Pro for Artists platform, letting artists sell lyric merchandise to fans, manage earnings through a new Wallet, and track how listeners engage with their lyrics via an analytics dashboard. The Bologna-based company says optional AI licensing is 'coming soon' to the Wallet, giving artists 'an additional opportunity to earn from the authorized use of their lyrics by AI platforms'. The platform is now used by more than 1.5 million artists.
articles.body: Musixmatch has launched a new version of its Musixmatch Pro for Artists platform, the Bologna-based company announced on Wednesday, November 25. The update lets artists sell lyric merchandise to fans via the Musixmatch app and website, adds a new Wallet for managing those earnings, merchandise sales and referrals in a single view, and adds an Insights & Analytics dashboard that combines streaming activity, follower data and lyric views across an artist's catalogue. 'Lyrics are one of the most powerful ways people connect with music, helping listeners discover artists and become lasting fans,' said Marco Paglia, Co-President at Musixmatch. 'With the enhanced Musixmatch Pro for Artists platform, we're providing new analytics to show artists how and where fans are engaging with their lyrics, and a brand new Wallet to help them earn from that engagement directly.' The platform's AI Enrichment tool transcribes lyrics and synchronises them line by line and word by word, and produces AI-generated meanings and themes for songs, which Musixmatch says can make them more visible across platforms. Artists will also have access to Music Lens, an AI agent Musixmatch unveiled in November 2025 that it says helps artists 'explore their catalogs and uncover new insights about their songs'. Musixmatch says optional AI licensing is 'coming soon' to the Wallet, giving artists 'an additional opportunity to earn from the authorized use of their lyrics by AI platforms', though its announcement did not name the AI platforms that would license lyrics through the Wallet or give a launch date for the feature. The planned AI licensing option follows deals Musixmatch signed in October 2025 with the publishing arms of all three major music companies — Sony Music Publishing, Universal Music Publishing Group and Warner Chappell Music — giving it access to catalogues of more than 15 million musical works. In October, Musixmatch also acquired Music Reports, the Los Angeles-based company behind the Songdex copyright registry, a deal it described as transforming it into 'a full-stack rights and royalties platform'. Musixmatch first announced Musixmatch Pro in July 2021, when more than 500,000 artists were managing their lyrics directly through the platform; in September it launched Musixmatch Pro for Labels, with more than 400 labels onboarded during the beta phase. Artists use the platform to transcribe and time-sync lyrics and distribute them to services including Spotify, Instagram, Apple Music, Amazon Music and Google.

articles.title: Saturday Night Live taps Amanda Seyfried, Robert De Niro and Timothée Chalamet as holiday hosts
articles.description: Saturday Night Live has lined up Amanda Seyfried, Robert De Niro and Timothée Chalamet to host its December holiday shows, with Don Toliver, Slayyyter and Charli XCX serving as musical guests during the month. The Christmas episodes are among the most-watched of the SNL season, and this year's line-up mixes film stars with pop acts. The announcement comes as the show heads into its annual run of festive episodes.
articles.body: Saturday Night Live has announced its holiday hosts: Amanda Seyfried, Robert De Niro and Timothée Chalamet will front the show's December episodes, with Don Toliver, Slayyyter and Charli XCX serving as musical guests during the month. The Christmas episodes are a fixture of the SNL calendar and among the most-watched shows of the season, mixing the programme's regular cast with big-name guests for festive sketches and musical performances. De Niro is a familiar face at Studio 8H, having appeared many times over the years, while Chalamet has become one of the show's favourite guests of recent seasons, and Seyfried returns to hosting duties. The musical line-up spans rap, hyperpop and mainstream pop: Don Toliver, who is currently on his Nitrous world tour; Slayyyter, the hyperpop artist whose profile has surged this year; and Charli XCX, one of pop's most in-demand live acts. The December run is also a key moment for SNL's current cast, with the holiday episodes traditionally drawing the season's biggest audiences and the most talked-about sketches. The hosts were announced on November 23, with the episodes set to air across December as the show builds toward its Christmas special.

articles.title: 'Ted Lasso' is coming back for season five
